name: Ninety-eight
description: 98: adding game. Play one card to a central pile and announce new total. A-9 add face value; 10 subtracts 10; J/Q no change; K sets pile to 98. Avoid exceeding 98; first to push total over 98 loses. Often played as drinking game.

Adding game; likely North American mid-20th century. Families reported playing 98 in the 1970s, 99 in the 1950s. Similar to 99 and 100 (same family).

items.text: UMass Amherst variant: Extra special cards: Ace of Clubs/Diamonds +1 or +11; Ace of Spades pick player to eliminate; Ace of Hearts blocks Spades and discard/draw; Four reverses direction; Nine counts zero and pass turn; Ten +10 or -10; King sets to 98; Queen of Spades exchange hands; other Queens and all Jacks +10.

98 Arizona version: Standard 52-card pack with two jokers. Four cards each; play to center pile. Ace +1 or +11; Nine reverses direction; Jack -10; Queen or Four zero; King sets to 98; Joker sets to 98 and next player must play twice on 98 or play other joker. Multiple cards of same rank may be played together (total value added); draw that many to refill. When stock runs out, play continues without replenishment until one player remains.
